itinerary.cal: Access is via ~38 miles of FS Road 51 from the town of Entiat; go after the road and high country are snow-free (typically July-October) and note this is Glacier Peak Wilderness, so wilderness group-size/camping rules apply.

days.note: From the Entiat River Trailhead, follow the Entiat River Trail about 7 miles to the 45-Mile Sheep Driveway, then climb off-trail via Aurora Creek into the Pinnacle Creek drainage below Borealis Ridge, gaining most of the day's elevation in the final push above treeline. Parties describe this as a long, ~10-11 hour carry with a full pack; camp is pitched wherever water and a flat spot align (common sites: ~6,500 ft in the Pinnacle Creek drainage, or up on the ~7,600 ft Borealis Ridge crest for a shorter summit day).
days.title: Backpack in to high camp (Entiat River Trail option)

schedule.label: Leave Entiat River Trailhead
schedule.detail: Northwest Forest Pass required; ~38 mi up FS Road 51 from the town of Entiat to reach the TH.

schedule.label: Clear the Entiat River Trail miles
schedule.detail: First 7 miles go quickly on good trail along the river.

schedule.label: Enter the Pinnacle Creek drainage / burn zone
schedule.detail: Trail quality degrades through old fire damage above the basin; open meadows and larches begin.

schedule.label: Make camp
schedule.detail: Common sites are ~6,500 ft in the Pinnacle Creek drainage or higher on Borealis Ridge (~7,600 ft) if you want a shorter summit day.

days.objective: Reach a high camp near Borealis Ridge / Pinnacle Creek below Pinnacle

days.note: An early, light-pack scramble to the summit and back to camp, followed by breaking camp and hiking all the way out the same day — reported as a very long ~10-11 hour, ~15-mile day but the standard way solo/2-day parties do it. The climb itself is an easy Class 2 walk/scramble on the south slopes from the crest saddle just south of the peak, though loose scree and talus make the last stretch tedious.
days.title: Summit push and hike out

schedule.label: Leave camp
schedule.detail: Light/day pack; climb from camp to the crest saddle just south of the peak.

schedule.label: Traverse the burn zone ridge
schedule.detail: Class 2 ridge travel with crappy scree underfoot; route stays below 8,000 ft until the final pitch.

schedule.label: Summit Pinnacle Mountain
schedule.detail: Final push up steep, loose scree/talus on the south slopes to the 8,400 ft summit.

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: Reverse the ascent route; break down camp and shoulder full pack.

schedule.label: Begin hike out
schedule.detail: Retrace the Entiat River Trail the full ~14-15 miles back to the car.

schedule.label: Reach trailhead
schedule.detail: A long finish; many parties are hiking the last miles in fading light.

days.objective: Climb Pinnacle Mountain (8,400 ft) then pack out to the trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 2-day, roughly 27-29 mile round trip with ~5,000-5,500 ft of total gain: a long backpack in via the Entiat River Trail to a high camp in the Pinnacle Creek drainage/Borealis Ridge, then an early summit scramble followed by a full hike-out the same day.
